note: These original records are preserved for later policy-compliant review; historical verification fields are not authenticated evidence and this file does not register capabilities.

limitations: the search covers every PUBLIC function in the stated file, in source order, because a sentence that named one function would have said which; a private function or a method is not searched unless it is named.
cases are the fuzzer's: annotation-directed draws plus a boundary corpus; an unannotated parameter gets int and str draws, which is what finds `add('', 0)` as a TypeError.
each case runs in its own interpreter with a wall-clock cap, so a hang or a segfault is an outcome that is reported, not a lost run.
an exception named in expected_exceptions is not a crash.
the shrink must keep the SAME failure mode; the reproduction is re-checked after shrinking and a changed mode is a refusal.
when nothing crashes the answer is 'NO CRASH REPRODUCED' with the number of functions searched and cases run -- that is a search result, not a pass.

limitations: the reference is stated or it comes from git (default HEAD); with neither, the call is REFUSED rather than compared against whatever file is nearby.
both implementations are loaded by file path under private module names, so a reference cannot shadow the code under test and two same-named packages cannot collide.
agreement means the same outcome and, for a return, the same repr; two equal exceptions agree even when their messages differ, because a message is prose.
the shrink must keep the same KIND of disagreement (value vs exception vs returns-vs-raises).
one child evaluates both sides over the whole case list for speed; if that child dies, the unreported cases are re-run one at a time so a crash is attributed to a side instead of losing the run.
a module that imports its own package relatively is reported NOT IMPORTABLE rather than silently compared as a stub.

limitations: cases are drawn from the parameter annotations plus a boundary corpus (0, 1, -1, sys.maxsize, '', 'a', '0'); an unannotated parameter gets int and str draws only, so a structured or generic input is not invented.
each case runs in its own interpreter with a wall-clock cap; timeout, nonzero exit and unparseable child output are all outcomes ('timeout', 'crashed', 'signaled'), never a lost run.
an exception is a finding only when it is not in expected_exceptions, because a validator that must raise is not a bug.
shrinking is greedy and must keep the SAME failure mode; a reduction that changes how it fails is rejected and the previous case is kept.
the reproducer is written beside the artifact as a standalone script; it is a record of the minimal call, not a regression test for the suite.
varargs / keyword-only targets are refused, because the arity is not knowable without running the code.

The wheel is copied to `<project>/dist/` so the caller can find it; the temporary wheelhouse is removed.

limitations: the growth class is a FIT over a measured ladder (default 64..2048), not a proof: `slope` and `r2` are reported and a class is claimed only when the log-log line is straight.
one child runs the whole ladder after a warm-up, because per-size process startup cost more than the call at small sizes; if that child dies the run is refused rather than half-timed.
the size is carried by one positional parameter (default index 0), as an int, or as a list of that length when the parameter is annotated as a list.
the minimum of the repetitions is kept, because one scheduler hiccup must not become a curve.

limitations: every case runs in its own interpreter, so a crash or a hang is an outcome and never a lost run, and the profiler never measures itself in the caller's process.
the reported hotspots are the WORST case's, not an average over all of them: an average ranks a function that is slow once beside one that is slow always.
the harness's own frames are filtered out, so the ranking cannot be topped by the profiler.
cProfile adds per-call overhead, which is why the ranking is by cumulative time and the absolute seconds are reported as measured rather than as a floor.

limitations: the measurement is tracemalloc's TRACED allocation, which is Python objects only; memory held by C extensions or the allocator's arenas is not counted.
the snapshot is taken while the returned value is still alive, because the bytes a call RETURNS are the interesting ones and a profile of freed intermediates measures the collector.
the ladder of sizes is always present (8, 64, 512) beside the annotated draws, because the fuzzer's boundary corpus tops out at 2**63 and a profile cannot finish it.
attribution is by allocating LINE through an 8-frame traceback; a single-frame traceback attributes everything to the caller and is a measured defect this adapter avoids.

limitations: a flake is proven by REPLAY, never by a linter: the verdict is outcome variance across runs, and the evidence for each flaky test names the exact order and hash seeds that failed.
the order-shuffling plugin is written to a temp dir, but tests execute with caller privileges against the source tree and can modify it; this is not a sandbox.
a test that fails in EVERY run is reported as consistently_failing, not as a flake, so a stable failure is not 'fixed' by rerunning.
stable means 'passed in every run of this budget'; a flake rarer than the run count is invisible, and detection_scope says so instead of certifying determinism.
duplicate JUnit identities are reduced to the worst outcome in each run; within-run variation is not detected, and reports can be tampered with by project code.
repeats below 2 refuses REPEATS_BELOW_TWO: one execution is a test run, not a flake hunt.

observed_effect.golden: a suite with one order-dependent test: 4 runs over 4 seeded collection orders report flakes_found=1, the flaky test named with per-run evidence (seed 0 passed, seeds 1-3 failed)
observed_effect.honesty: repeats<2 refuses REPEATS_BELOW_TWO; no tests refuses NO_TESTS_FOUND; a collection error refuses TESTS_COULD_NOT_RUN instead of reporting zero flakes
observed_effect.scope: the tree is byte-untouched by the probe (the shuffle plugin lives in a temp dir on PYTHONPATH)
observed_effect.stable: the order-independent test in the same suite is in `stable`, and a test that fails in every run appears in `consistently_failing` rather than `flaky_tests`

limitations: a same-scope static reading: a with-statement, a close/terminate/kill/release call on the bound name in the same scope, or returning the handle clears a finding; it does not claim path-sensitivity, so a handle closed on one branch and leaked on another is not reported.

builtins/io open, socket.socket, socket.create_connection, sqlite3.connect, subprocess.Popen, os.popen, tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile, tarfile.open, zipfile.ZipFile, urllib.request.urlopen and mmap.mmap are the acquisitions it knows; a wrapper with its own close() is not assumed to be one of them.
a resource acquired in one function and closed in another is reported: scopes are analysed separately.

limitations: the engine is detect-secrets: 27 detectors and an entropy filter, with the providers Yelp ships. A credential shape no detector knows is not found; the artifact says which detectors ran.
findings carry a salted SHA-1 and a location, never the secret itself -- a report that quotes the credential is a second leak.
verification against the provider (`is_verified`) is OFF: it would send the credential to a third party. The artifact says so per finding.
the scan covers every file in the tree, not only git-tracked ones; binary files are skipped by detect-secrets' own rules.
TOOL_NOT_INSTALLED:detect-secrets is refused by name rather than reported as zero findings -- an empty report from a scanner that did not run is a lie.

limitations: the advisory source is pip-audit's PyPI service: every finding carries a PYSEC id with its CVE/GHSA aliases and the versions that fix it. Without network there is no advisory data, and the verb refuses ADVISORY_SERVICE_UNREACHABLE rather than reporting zero -- an empty report from a service that was never reached is a lie.

the audited set is the project's OWN declaration: [project].dependencies from pyproject.toml, else requirements*.txt, else a stated requirements_path. It is resolved by pip, so a floating range audits the version pip would install today.
a requirements_path that does not exist is refused by name; pip resolution conflicts are refused as ADVISORY_SERVICE_UNREACHABLE with pip's own words, because the run could not happen.
this audits declared dependencies, not the running interpreter: use the project, not the venv, as the target.
